title: U.S. House · California's 39th District
area: Western Riverside County, including Riverside, Moreno Valley, and Perris.

context.text: California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary. Incumbent Mark Takano (D) and Steve Manos (R) were the only two candidates to advance to the November general election.

summary.text: Mark Takano is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 39th District, serving on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.

background.text: Born in Riverside, California, in 1960; earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard University in 1983 and a Master of Fine Arts in creative writing from the University of California, Riverside in 2010.
Worked as a teacher before his election to Congress in 2012.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the House Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

summary.text: Steve Manos is a business owner and the mayor of Lake Elsinore, California, running as a Republican for California's 39th Congressional District under the campaign theme 'Faith, Family, and Affordability.'

background.text: Has lived in the Inland Empire since 1987; a business owner since 1996 and past president of the Inland Valleys Association of Realtors.

Elected to the Lake Elsinore City Council in 2012 and has served as mayor of Lake Elsinore in 2015, 2019, 2024, and 2026; also serves as a director of the Riverside County Habitat Conservation Authority and the Southern California Association of Governments.

priorities.text: Campaign platform is 'Faith, Family, and Affordability': he says he would protect parental rights, remove regulatory barriers that raise housing costs, fund freeway repairs along the 215 corridor, support veterans, and limit government overreach.

positions.summary: Says the district's greatest need is affordable, market-rate housing and calls for removing regulatory barriers that increase housing costs.
positions.quote: Our greatest need is affordable, market-rate housing for our young and young-at-heart.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in California, 2026

researchNotes: Takano has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current campaign-issues page was found, so no current stated priorities/positions are cited for him beyond his official committee record. Manos has not completed a Candidate Connection survey either; his priorities/positions are drawn from his campaign website.
